title: R' Levi bar Zavda
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites the Venice printing of Tanchuma, Bechukotai, as mentioning him expounding the verse quoted here as ‘I will go, and you descended upon the mountains’: ‘Do people descend? Do they not ascend?’ etc. Hyman reports that other printings read ‘R' Zecharyah said’; he gives the Buber Tanchuma reading as R' Levi bar Berechyah.

notes.text: The supplied quotation reads אלך וירדת, mixing “I will go” with “you descended.” Its intended wording remains unresolved; it is not silently replaced with a biblical verse.

Supplied אלך וירדת mixes I will go with you descended; it is not silently changed to an imperative or a newly selected biblical verse. The cited Venice TanchumaBechukotai passage was not obtained in the earlier finite searches, which do not prove universal absence. Other-printings Zecharyah and Buber Levi bar Berechyah remain Hyman’s reported variants, not newly checked editions. All these personal titles are supplied only as abbreviations and stay R'. Heading Zavda and body Zevida are conventional transliteration choices, not two newly bound identities.

The consulted Tanchuma, Bechukotai 5, attributes the homily to R’ Zecharyah. The Buber text, Bechukotai 7, gives R’ Levi ben Berechyah, while Hyman gives bar. Both quote Judges 11:37 with the first-person ‘I will go and descend’ and interpret the mountains as the Sanhedrin. Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 858) has the mixed-person wording translated in the body. The reading of the Venice printing he cites remains unverified.
